assessment: Overall, the retained passages preserve the book’s chronological and argumentative arc: the motive and practical framing in Economy and Where I Lived; the epistemic and moral practices (Reading; Sounds; Solitude; Brute Neighbors; The Bean-Field); representative seasonal and natural evidence (The Ponds; The Pond in Winter; Spring); explicit moral theory (Higher Laws); a clear concluding synthesis (Conclusion); and the political corollary in On the Duty of Civil Disobedience. The selection maintains the experiment’s demonstrative cases (cabin, bean-field, foraging) and preserves the connective philosophical material that links private practice to public conscience. Stylistically memorable aphorisms and programmatic definitional sentences are largely present, and the Project Gutenberg license is retained for provenance.
missing_coverage: CH004-K01-B03 — The canonical Economy passage that contains the famous aphorism about 'the mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation' and the fullest sociological/moral diagnosis of labor’s spiritual cost. This is a core rhetorical and argumentative hinge for the book’s critique of conventional livelihood and must be included to represent the governing thesis faithfully.

CH022-K01-B16 — The concrete tax-gatherer encounter (the practical scene of Thoreau’s resistance). Although an arrest anecdote appears in CH011, the tax-gatherer episode in the Civil Disobedience essay provides the direct tactical exemplar that roots the argumentative prescriptions in lived praxis.

CH022-K01-B17 — The sustained argument that imprisonment is the proper place for just men under an unjust government and the discussion of the moral power of conscientious imprisonment. This tactical and moral analysis is a key consequence of the essay’s core claim and clarifies how noncooperation functions strategically.

transition_notes.note: Insert CH004-K01-B03 (the central ‘quiet desperation’ passage) here to ensure the Economy section retains its canonical sociological diagnosis and rhetorical center before the bean-field empirical material.

Place CH022-K01-B16 (tax-gatherer encounter) and then CH022-K01-B17 (argument about prison as the proper place for just men) prior to the existing summary sentence 'This is the whole history of "My Prisons."' so that the practical exemplars precede the reflective closure.
